definitions.gloss: eating while walking; eating on the go
definitions.explanation: The act of eating food while walking around, especially street food at festivals or tourist areas.
Visiting multiple restaurants, food stalls, or shops in an area to sample different dishes. A popular leisure activity in Japan.

examples.japanese: {商店街|しょうてんがい}で{食|た}べ{歩|ある}きした。
examples.english: I ate while walking through the shopping street.

examples.japanese: お{祭|まつ}りの{食|た}べ{歩|ある}きが{楽|たの}しい。
examples.english: Eating while walking around at the festival is fun.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}で{食|た}べ{歩|ある}きが{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: Eating while walking has become a problem in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {築地|つきじ}で{食|た}べ{歩|ある}きをした。
examples.english: I went on a food tour in Tsukiji.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}と{食|た}べ{歩|ある}きの{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てた。
examples.english: I made a food tour plan with my friends.

examples.japanese: ラーメンの{食|た}べ{歩|ある}きブログを{書|か}いている{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many people who write ramen restaurant-hopping blogs.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 (eating while walking) can be considered rude in some contexts in Japan, especially in residential areas or near temples. Sense 2 (food touring) is a popular leisure activity, often featured in travel guides and TV shows.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {食|た}べ{歩|ある}きグルメ (street food, walking-around food)
- {食|た}べ{歩|ある}きマップ (food tour map)
- {食|た}べ{歩|ある}き{禁止|きんし} (no eating while walking)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Some tourist areas in Japan have posted {食|た}べ{歩|ある}き{禁止|きんし} signs to address litter and congestion. Despite this, {食|た}べ{歩|ある}き remains a key part of visiting famous food streets like {築地|つきじ} and {錦市場|にしきいちば}.
